subject: Throughput sizing follow-up: Finex Payments (post-demo)
messages:
From: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Li <alex.li@finexpay.com>, Samir Gupta <samir.gupta@finexpay.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 2 Mar 2026 16:12:00 -0700
Subject: Post-demo recap + throughput details we discussed

Hi Alex / Samir —

Thanks again for the time today — good discussion on the fraud-detection assistant and live guidance flows. Per our zoom, wanted to capture the follow-ups we agreed on so we can validate sizing and propose a configuration that hits your latency SLOs while keeping costs predictable.

Quick recap of what I have so far from the call:
- Use case: real-time decisioning + agent-style guidance for customer support (short prompts + multi-turn context).
- Preferred model family: you mentioned starting with an Llama-3-class open model (we can validate with a Redwood-verified variant).
- Streaming: you need progressive token streaming to the UI (first-token latency matters).

Requested from your side (items you said you'd confirm):
1) Steady-state QPS and expected peak QPS (including duration of peaks).
2) Average and 95th-percentile tokens per request (input + output).
3) Concurrency (how many concurrent user sessions/streams during peaks).
4) First-token latency SLO (p95/p99) and acceptable total response latency.
5) Whether you can accept quantized models (4-bit/8-bit) for cost reasons, or need FP16.

Next steps from our side: once we get the numbers above we'll run a quick throughput sizing estimate (tokens/sec, required concurrent model replicas, and recommended Dedicated configuration). If it looks close we'll schedule a short benchmarks session where you send a small sample workload (CSV) and our infra team runs an internal sim.

If you can reply with the numbers in-line below, that would be perfect.

Thanks —
Rafael
Account Exec | Redwood Inference
rafael.mendes@redwood.ai | +1-415-555-0182

Attachment: finex_workload_sample.csv (placeholder)

From: Alex Li <alex.li@finexpay.com>
To: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.ai>
Cc: Samir Gupta <samir.gupta@finexpay.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 4 Mar 2026 09:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-demo recap + throughput details we discussed

Hi Rafael —

Thanks — below are the numbers Samir and I pulled together after the demo. I attached a small sample of session traces (finex_workload_sample.csv) showing request timestamps + token counts. Summary below:

1) Steady-state QPS: ~20 qps (normal business hours)
2) Peak QPS: up to 280 qps during heavy traffic windows (approx 5–10 minutes per spike, several times per day)
3) Average tokens per request: input ~80 tokens, output ~320 tokens (so ~400 tokens total avg)
4) 95th percentile tokens per request: ~750 total tokens (longer troubleshooting responses)
5) Concurrency: steady ~40 concurrent streams, peak instantaneous concurrency ~600 (many short-lived sessions during peak)
6) Streaming: yes — we stream tokens to the frontend; we need first-token streaming (progressive render)
7) Latency SLOs: first-token p95 <= 200ms, p99 <= 400ms; total response p95 <= 600ms, p99 <= 1.2s (we can tolerate longer tails during rare system maintenance windows)
8) Model requirements: prefer an open model you verified; willing to try 8-bit quantization but would like to validate quality on our eval set (we'll share eval prompts).

Extra context: most requests are short guidance/resolution steps (2–6 turns), but occasionally we generate longer, templated responses for dispute letters which drive the 750-token 95th. Peak bursts correlate with batch reconciliation jobs that trigger many webhook-driven lookups.

We attached our SLA doc (finex_sla_requirements.pdf) with the internal thresholds. Let us know if you need any more detail.

Thanks —
Alex Li
Head of Product, Finex Payments
alex.li@finexpay.com

From: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Li <alex.li@finexpay.com>, Samir Gupta <samir.gupta@finexpay.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 5 Mar 2026 08:14:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-demo recap + throughput details we discussed

Appreciate the details, Alex — this is exactly what we need. A couple of quick clarifying questions before we run a sizing pass:

- For the "first-token" SLOs you listed, is that measured from request arrival at your client (so includes network + our edge) or measured from when Redwood starts model execution? We typically size assuming end-to-end (client->first-token).
- For the 600 concurrent peak, is that mostly short-lived (<= 30s) or can sessions remain active for minutes? This affects KV cache utilization and memory pressure.
- For the 95th-token-length (750 tokens), do you have a rough split input/output? (E.g., 200 in / 550 out).

Proposed next steps:
1) If you confirm the clarifications above, we'll produce an initial tokens/sec sizing (steady vs peak) and recommended Dedicated pool (GPU type + replica count + concurrency configs).
2) Schedule a 60-minute bench run next week where we replay your sample CSV against a couple of model variants (8-bit quantized + FP16) to validate latency and output quality.

We can block time for the bench; Marissa / Vivek from infra will join to define the benchmark harness. Would next Wednesday (Mar 11) morning PST work for a 60-minute slot?

Best —
Rafael

(Internal note: loop in Vivek now for sizing guidance)

From: Samir Gupta <samir.gupta@finexpay.com>
To: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.ai>, Alex Li <alex.li@finexpay.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 5 Mar 2026 09:24:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-demo recap + throughput details we discussed

Thanks Rafael — quick answers from our infra/ops side:

- First-token SLOs are measured at the client (end-to-end). That is the number that matters for UX.
- Peak concurrent sessions: ~600 but they are typically very short-lived (median session length ~12s during spikes). We do have longer sessions (minutes) but they are the minority.
- For the 750-token 95th, split is roughly input 180 / output 570.

We're happy to run the benchmark next Wed (Mar 11) at 10:00 AM PST. I'll share a temporary SSH / API endpoint for the replay harness and we've uploaded the sample CSV to the drive link Rafael included.

Also: please include a sizing calc in your next email that shows tokens/sec math for steady vs peak (i.e., qps * avg tokens and qps * 95th tokens) and an estimated number of concurrent model replicas for a 200ms first-token p95 target and streaming. That will help us evaluate cost.

Samir
CTO, Finex Payments
